architecture.purpose: Express authentication/authorization and service routing hub
architecture.database: mysql2/promise connection pool; pool.execute returns rows through custom db.query

roles.0: default in admin createUser when role omitted; not documented consistently

architecture.authentication: Bearer JWT required; current user role and active state re-read from DB on every request; password hashes bcryptjs for regular auth and bcrypt for admin
architecture.jwt_lifetimes: Registration/login JWT_EXPIRE or 24h; admin login hard-coded 7d; no refresh/logout/revocation implementation
architecture.csrf: Server-side synchronizer token stored in Map per userID:IP; 32 random bytes as 64 hex characters, 1h expiry, cleanup every 10min; safe methods exempt
middleware_order: routes: auth, role guard where present, API logging, CSRF, handler
architecture.proxy_trust: trust proxy=1; custom IP parsers also directly trust forwarded headers
architecture.internal_routing: Mostly HTTP upstream requests with x-internal-auth; authenticated userID appended after client fields so caller cannot override it; upload is exception using only x-user-id.

findings.title: Admin log routes have no admin authorization
findings.detail: The /api/logs mount requires a valid user but not role 1. Every /admin/* log endpoint also omits adminMiddleware and controllers never check roles. Any active user can reach global searches, another user's logs, security alerts, system statistics and destructive cleanup. Existing DB-result bugs do not make this safe: search returns the first matching row as an object and cleanup runs DELETE before throwing.
findings.remediation: Apply adminMiddleware to the complete /api/logs/admin router before handlers; verify role 2 and 3 receive 403, including cleanup.

findings.title: Log APIs assume the wrong db.query return shape
findings.detail: The DB wrapper returns rows directly, not mysql2's [rows, fields]. Log helpers and controller destructure const [logs], const [stats], const [countResult], etc. getMyLogs/getAllLogs dereference countResult[0] on a row object; stats/security attempt reduce on a row object or undefined; cleanup destructures a non-iterable ResultSetHeader after DELETE has already committed. Most log APIs therefore fail or return a single malformed row.

evidence.excerpt: const [countResult] = await db.query('SELECT COUNT(*) as total FROM api_logs');

findings.remediation: Keep a single DB wrapper contract and remove the extra destructuring in all log readers/deleters; verify result arrays, empty sets, counts and affectedRows.

findings.title: CAPTCHA answers are delivered as machine-readable SVG text
findings.detail: generateCaptchaSVG emits the actual six answer characters as ordered SVG text nodes. The response is merely base64 SVG, so a program can read the answer without OCR. Distortion, curves and noise do not prevent extraction from the document. This defeats the compulsory registration CAPTCHA and login challenge.
findings.remediation: Use an established challenge service or rasterize text server-side into an image that does not include accessible answer text; use cryptographic randomness.

findings.title: Client IP security relies on unconditionally trusted headers
findings.detail: CAPTCHA/login attempt/block helpers accept X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP directly; CSRF and audit helpers additionally accept CF-Connecting-IP directly. These values are not checked against the connecting reverse proxy. If the application is directly reachable or the ingress forwards client-supplied headers, clients can choose their block/captcha/audit identity. Express trust proxy = 1 also requires an actual single trusted ingress. Different helpers use different header priority, so auth, CSRF and rate limits can disagree on the same request's IP.
findings.certainty: confirmed trust issue; external exploitability depends on ingress configuration
findings.remediation: Define trusted proxy addresses, keep the gateway inaccessible directly when appropriate, normalize one client-IP function from validated proxy information, and have ingress overwrite forwarding headers.

findings.title: Password-change logs include both plaintext passwords
findings.detail: changePassword calls maskSensitiveData({currentPassword,newPassword}) and prints the result. maskSensitiveData's allowlist of sensitive names contains password but neither currentPassword nor newPassword, so both values remain unchanged in server logs. The API logger has a separate shallow list and does not redact currentPassword either.
findings.remediation: Do not log password-change request values. Centralize recursive redaction including currentPassword/newPassword and remove existing sensitive logs according to retention requirements.

findings.title: Malformed CSRF header causes 500 instead of controlled rejection
findings.detail: crypto.timingSafeEqual throws when buffer lengths differ. csrfProtection does not validate that the supplied header is a 64-character hexadecimal token or compare buffer lengths first, so a malformed authenticated request reaches the global error handler and receives 500.
findings.remediation: Validate header type/format and equal byte lengths before timingSafeEqual; return 403 for every invalid token.

findings.title: CSRF token storage prevents reliable multi-tab or multi-instance use
findings.detail: Only one token is retained for each userID:IP. Every GET token request replaces it, invalidating other tabs/devices behind the same IP. Tokens disappear on process restart and are not shared across workers, so requests can fail randomly behind a load balancer. The implementation is a server-side synchronizer token, despite comments calling it double-submit; there is no cookie comparison.
findings.remediation: Use stable session-scoped tokens in a shared store or an appropriate signed stateless design; avoid invalidating an existing valid token every time it is requested.

findings.title: CSRF and session audit columns are never populated accurately
findings.detail: apiLogger reads req.csrfTokenValid before csrfProtection runs; csrfProtection never writes that property at all. req.user has no sessionId. All logged requests therefore have null csrf_token_valid and session_id, even when a CSRF check passes or fails.

evidence.excerpt: const csrfTokenValid = req.csrfTokenValid !== undefined ? req.csrfTokenValid : null;

findings.remediation: Capture CSRF result when the response finishes, explicitly set pass/fail in the CSRF middleware, and define a session identifier only if the authentication design has sessions.

findings.title: Database audit logging misses auth failures and rate-limit rejections
findings.detail: Public auth/captcha/admin-login and token endpoints do not attach apiLogger. Protected routes run authMiddleware and role checks before logger, and the global limiter runs even earlier. Login/register/password changes and unauthenticated/forbidden/global-rate-limit requests are therefore absent from api_logs despite event classification code for them.
findings.remediation: Install a request-finish audit hook early enough to observe rejects, while taking user identity at finish and aggressively redacting bodies.

findings.title: Audit request paths lose the API prefix
findings.detail: apiLogger captures req.path inside path-mounted middleware. Express has already trimmed that mount prefix, so /api/admin/users is recorded as /users and several unrelated roots as /. The event classifier also uses req.path rather than req.originalUrl/baseUrl, undermining /admin, /send-image and /zalo-accounts classification.
findings.remediation: Record a normalized path from req.originalUrl and classify from that captured full path; keep query values separate and sanitized.

findings.title: CAPTCHA verification is not bound to the issuing IP or atomic use
findings.detail: The verifier accepts an ip argument and stores ipAddress during creation, but its SELECT only checks captchaID, purpose, isUsed and expiry. It never compares stored IP. SELECT and UPDATE are separate, unguarded operations, so concurrent requests can both validate one challenge before either marks it used.

evidence.excerpt: 'UPDATE captcha_sessions SET isUsed = TRUE WHERE captchaID = ?',

findings.remediation: Bind a challenge to its intended session/context and atomically consume it with a guarded update or transaction/row lock.

findings.title: CAPTCHA answers and submitted values are printed in every environment
findings.detail: Unconditional debug logging prints the plaintext generated answer and user-submitted answer, plus hashes and full challenge/session information. NODE_ENV does not gate these messages.
findings.remediation: Remove answer/input debug output and log only non-sensitive challenge outcomes.

findings.title: Mandatory environment configuration is dereferenced before validation
findings.detail: Several modules execute process.env.DOCKER_HOST.trim() at import time, so a missing value throws before the server can start. MAIN_SERVER_PORT/host, DB values, JWT_SECRET and rate-limit numbers have no complete startup validation. No original .env or package manifest was included in recovered source at this analysis stage.
findings.remediation: Supply a documented local .env, validate required values and numeric ranges before importing dependent modules, and use explicit safe defaults where intended.

findings.title: No readiness validation or automatic core schema initialization
findings.detail: startServer calls app.listen without db.testConnection or schema migrations. /health returns success unconditionally. database.js only defines fb_setup DDL and exports initFbSetup; MAIN never invokes it. The other tables and both log views must already exist, so a green /health does not demonstrate that login or admin APIs work.
findings.remediation: Provide explicit migrations/schema and a readiness check that verifies database connectivity and required migrations, while retaining a lightweight liveness route.

findings.title: Admin self-update checks have type and omission bugs
findings.detail: When updating the current admin, userRole !== 1 rejects requests that omit userRole, even though later code treats it as optional. Self-lock protection only recognizes numeric 0; boolean false or string 0 can pass and persist an inactive account. Incoming role, active flag and balance are otherwise not validated.
findings.remediation: Normalize and validate role/boolean/money fields once, then apply self-protection only to explicitly provided normalized changes.

findings.title: License extension can concatenate strings and lose concurrent updates
findings.detail: count is only checked for truthiness and count < 1, so numeric strings and fractional values are accepted. license.countDown + count concatenates a string count instead of adding numerically. The result is assigned to undeclared global newCountDown and written using read-modify-write without a transaction, allowing concurrent extensions to overwrite one another.

evidence.excerpt: const { count } = req.body; // Số tháng gia hạn

findings.remediation: Validate a finite positive integer and use an atomic UPDATE countDown = countDown + ? with a scoped result variable.

findings.title: Product statistics uses inconsistent license fields
findings.detail: getProductStats counts licenseID and aggregates license.isActivated/license.pricePaid, while the license screens and updates use status/countDown and store purchase price in user_link_license. Without the original schema it cannot be proved which fields exist; on a schema matching the other handlers this endpoint will fail or report stale/wrong totals. Adding compatibility columns alone does not synchronize them.
findings.certainty: confirmed inconsistency; actual missing-column error depends on unavailable original schema

evidence.excerpt: SUM(CASE WHEN l.isActivated = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as activatedLicenses,

findings.remediation: Confirm the original schema and derive per-product activated counts from status and revenue from purchase records consistently.

findings.title: Multi-step destructive operations are not transactional
findings.detail: deleteLicense removes user_link_license rows and then deletes the license in a separate query; failure of the second statement leaves the purchase links missing. deleteProduct checks for licenses and then deletes/updates without a transaction, leaving a race with purchases. DB transaction helpers exist but are unused by these controllers.

evidence.excerpt: await db.query('DELETE FROM user_link_license WHERE licenseKey = ?', [licenseKey]);
const sql = 'DELETE FROM license WHERE licenseKey = ?';

findings.remediation: Use transactions and the appropriate foreign keys/locking; make deletions and product availability checks consistent with purchase transactions.

findings.title: Global rate limiter exempts all auth and admin routes
findings.detail: globalLimiter skips any path starting /api/admin or /api/auth. Only the two login routes attach loginLimiter. Registration, profile and password-change endpoints, plus admin data/mutation routes, have no request limiter at this layer. CAPTCHA generation has its own 10/minute limit but the SVG answer is extractable.
findings.remediation: Define route-specific limits for registration, credential changes and expensive admin operations; avoid blanket prefix exemptions.

findings.title: Password changes do not revoke existing JWTs
findings.detail: Authentication verifies JWT signature/expiry and checks only user existence/isActive. changePassword only updates the password hash. An already-issued token remains valid after password reset until its original expiry, including the admin login's fixed 7-day token. There is no implemented logout, refresh, revocation list or token version.

evidence.excerpt: 'SELECT userID, userName, email, userRole, isActive FROM user WHERE userID = ?',

findings.remediation: If password changes are intended to end other sessions, introduce token-version/session revocation and increment/revoke it on credential changes.

findings.title: New-account and credential input validation is incomplete
findings.detail: Registration checks only presence of userName/password/email, then hashes and inserts; it does not enforce a minimum password length, email shape, string types or length bounds. Password change enforces length >= 6 but not a complete type contract. Admin creation similarly has only presence checks and defaults an omitted role to 0 although registration uses role 2.
findings.remediation: Use shared schemas for string type/length/email/role validation and consistent policy for registration, admin creation and password changes.

findings.title: Global leak-history lookup sends an array to one prepared placeholder
findings.detail: getGlobalLeakHistory executes WHERE userID IN (?) with [userIDs]. The DB wrapper uses mysql2 pool.execute prepared statements, which do not expand a JavaScript array into an IN list. For non-empty multi-user history this can throw or fail to match intended IDs.
findings.certainty: confirmed prepared-statement contract mismatch; exact error depends on mysql2/server versions

evidence.excerpt: 'SELECT userID, userName FROM user WHERE userID IN (?)',

findings.remediation: Generate one placeholder per validated user ID, or use an explicitly supported set-valued SQL mechanism; keep values bound individually.

findings.title: PayOS forwarding has no timeout
findings.detail: The create, history and cancel Axios calls have no timeout. A stalled payment upstream can keep requests open indefinitely. Return/cancel URLs also always use the first CORS_ORIGIN rather than the actual allowed origin selected for the user.
findings.remediation: Set bounded upstream deadlines/cancellation and explicitly configure the user-facing payment return URL.

findings.title: Link thumbnail upload buffers files without a limit
findings.detail: The admin-only link upload uses multer.memoryStorage without file-size or file-type limits. Even an accidental large upload can consume server memory. The regular PNG upload has a 3 MiB limit, but trusts client-provided MIME metadata rather than file bytes.
findings.remediation: Set explicit per-file/part limits and validate decoded image content; avoid unbounded in-memory buffering.

findings.title: Upload proxy does not propagate internal authentication
findings.detail: Most service proxy requests carry x-internal-auth. The file-upload proxy sends only multipart headers and x-user-id, so FILES_SERVER cannot authenticate this call using the shared secret from this request. If FILES_SERVER relies only on x-user-id and is reachable directly, callers can impersonate users. Exact downstream behavior is outside this MAIN analysis.
findings.certainty: confirmed missing header; downstream exposure requires FILES_SERVER/ingress review
findings.remediation: Use authenticated internal service-to-service requests and ensure FILES_SERVER validates caller identity before trusting x-user-id.

findings.title: Pagination and cleanup retention bounds are not enforced
findings.detail: Log limit/offset/days and daysToKeep are parsed without positive bounds or maximum values. Negative retention days select a future threshold and may delete recent/all logs; very large limits allow expensive responses. License list limits have a lower bound but no upper bound.
findings.remediation: Validate positive bounded integers, use a fixed safe retention policy or explicit validated range, and cap page sizes.

findings.title: Initial tool-setup insertion replaces explicit zero prices with defaults
findings.detail: updateToolSetup permits zero in validation but initial INSERT uses value || default for each fee. A requested free fee is silently replaced by a nonzero default when no setup row exists. Subsequent UPDATE preserves zero, making behavior depend on whether setup was initialized.
findings.remediation: Use explicit undefined/null fallback or nullish coalescing so valid zero values persist.

findings.title: CAPTCHA and block checks fail open on database errors
findings.detail: isCaptchaRequired returns false and isIPBlocked returns {blocked:false} on database exceptions. A missing captcha/login/IP-block table can disable extra login protection while ordinary user-table login still works. recordLoginAttempt also catches and ignores its write error, so counters can silently stop working.
findings.remediation: Treat unavailable security state explicitly: fail closed for the affected authentication operation or use a clearly designed fallback, and validate security tables during startup.

findings.title: General timer mount bypasses the VIP card-scheduling guard
findings.detail: The same timer router is mounted at /api/send-image-by-card-timer with authVipAndLog and at /api/zalo-timer with only authAndLog. Both expose POST /send. The handler chooses /api/schedule/card for every base URL not containing v2, so a regular role-2 user can reach the same card scheduling upstream through POST /api/zalo-timer/send. MAIN therefore does not enforce the intended VIP/admin gate consistently; a separate upstream check would be needed to prevent actual scheduling.
findings.certainty: confirmed gateway authorization bypass; successful scheduling additionally depends on missing timer upstream
findings.remediation: Mount only read-only history at the general timer path, or apply the VIP/admin guard to its scheduling handler; enforce the same rule upstream.

verification_limits: Static inspection only: no external provider/network calls, source execution, production DB or real user data were used.
Dependencies versions are unknown because no original package manifest/lockfile was recovered.
Missing upstream functions cannot be verified through a successful MAIN health response.
Some issues depend on original schema/ingress versions; those findings explicitly state that uncertainty.
No source edits made by this analysis task; the parent handles runtime setup.
